criteria.criterion: The diff in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs does not make the stub log starts in an expected order (no gate that holds a start entry until earlier entries exist), does not raise a timeout, add #[ignore] or delete the test.
criteria.evidence: The diff touches only lines 8525-8541, inside the test body. The `Shared` stub's `run()` (lines 8305-8346) is unchanged. No timeout is raised, no #[ignore] is added, and the test still exists.

criteria.criterion: The test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs still asserts 8 starts, at most two non-Steward starts in a row, improvement_turns equal to s1, s2, and an order check that fails if s1 is misplaced: either report.plan_groups.concat() equals u1..u6,s1,s2, or s1's start index is at least 4 with 3 workers (verifiable by reading the assertions against take_until_done in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs).
criteria.evidence: Lines 8529-8541 now assert that plan_groups.concat() equals u1..u6,s1,s2 and that s1's index in the start log is at least 4. The bound of 4 follows from the code. In take_until_done (drain.rs:2770), a worker pops an item and then runs it; the stub's run() logs `start` before that worker pops again. s1 is the 7th pop. The worker that pops it has already logged its previous start, and each of the other two workers holds at most one item it has popped but not yet logged. So at least 4 urgent starts come before s1. If the drain popped from the back, s1 would land at index 2 or earlier and the check would fail. The named-turn loop is unchanged and still asserts s1 among the first three starts, at most two non-s starts in a row, 8 starts, and taken turns == [s1, s2]. That loop is deterministic: plan.rs:2242-2265 shows the groups [u1,u2],[s1],[u3,u4],[s2],[u5,u6], and the groups run one after another.

criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new Fixed entry naming the test, a cause stated in terms of drain.rs worker pop-then-log behavior, a failure example the drain and stub can produce (s1 not in the first four log entries is impossible; example shows s1 at index 4 or 5 versus the old assertion), the jobs 20261029-204942-2zqw, 20261111-213010-8jgz and 20261029-233047-ab43, and a plain statement that a never-finishing run was not reproduced.

It gives the example log [u1,u2,u3,u4,s1,u5,u6,s2], with s1 at index 4, which the old six-urgent-first check rejects. It lists all three jobs. It says plainly: 'A run of this test that never finished was not reproduced either'.

findings.summary: The plan_groups assertion checks the plan's order, not what the drain actually handed out; the comment overstates it
findings.evidence: Report.plan_groups is `plan.groups` (drain.rs:3281), which the plan builds. It is not recorded from take_until_done's pops, so a pop-order bug in the drain would still pass this check. Detecting a wrong drain order rests on the s1_at >= 4 check, which does catch it. The comment 'The order the drain itself hands items out in' should say 'the plan order the drain dispatches from'.

summary: The change passes: all six criteria are met and there are no blocker or major findings. It fixes the flaky urgent-group drain test without weakening what it checks. The old check required s1 to be absent from the first six starts. That check could fail even when the drain was correct: a worker can pop u5 or u6 and not yet log its start when another worker pops s1 and logs it first. The test now asserts the plan order (u1..u6, s1, s2) and that s1's start index is at least 4. Reading take_until_done in drain.rs confirms that 4 always holds, and the check still fails if the drain hands s1 out early. The stub, the eight-start check, the two-in-a-row check and the improvement-turn checks are unchanged, and the named-turn half is deterministic because its groups run one after another. The targeted test passed in 0.02s, and Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed in CI. Only drain.rs tests and CHANGELOG.md changed. The changelog entry covers everything criterion 4 asks for. Three minor findings: the comment on the plan_groups assertion overstates what it checks; the flake was explained from the code rather than reproduced, as the entry admits; and in my 64-thread run a different, unchanged test (every_landing_path_ends_in_reinstall_for_any_unreadable_config) failed. That test may be another cause of the CI shard failures and needs its own job.
